topIssues.title: MemCode plugin for approved agent memory across elizaOS channels
topIssues.author: vivekgupta-memcode
topIssues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
An elizaOS agent can meet the same person through different channels, but a channel session alone does not express which user-approved facts should persist across them.

**Describe the solution you would like**
I’m Vivek Gupta, Founder & CEO of MemCode (https://memcode.in). I would like to contribute a plugin that uses the user’s authorization to recall a bounded set of relevant facts and offers explicit save, correct, and forget actions. Channel IDs would be mapped to the user on the server side. A first PR could include an example agent and tests for user separation and revoked access.

**Describe alternatives you have considered**
A standalone external plugin or MCP recipe may fit better than a first-party plugin. Existing runtime records and local storage would remain available; no full transcript would be copied automatically.

**Additional context**
Would maintainers prefer this in the first-party plugin structure or outside this repository? I can build the version you recommend.

**Evidence / expected proof for implementation**
A PR would include tests for user and channel scoping, a demonstration of the recall and explicit save flow, and logs or trajectory evidence where required. UI screenshots and video are N/A unless the chosen approach adds a UI.

cc @NubsCarson for your thoughts on this integration.

topPRs.title: Manage saved Reminders in Automations without adding them to Todos
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Saved Reminders appeared among owner Todos and had no dedicated management filter in Automations. Keep reminder records out of the Todo projection and expose them through a Reminders filter in the existing Automations page, without another launcher, scheduler or storage model.

The owner-scoped read projection includes saved messages, exact due times and recorded delivery outcomes. Existing definition/occurrence APIs handle message and one-shot due edits, eligible snoozes, and reversible cancellation by archival. Delivered reminders do not offer unsupported snooze/redelivery controls. Unknown or failed statuses are not labeled Scheduled; an unknown filter count is omitted rather than shown as zero. Other Automations content remains available.

Validation on pinned develop: 26 UI tests and two real PGlite/API integration tests passed, including foreign-owner isolation, retained records/plans, Todo exclusion, message-edit propagation into the existing body formatter, and registered route handling. UI and personal-assistant typechecks passed after current core and cloud-sdk builds. Focused formatting and diff checks passed. These checks do not claim actual notification delivery, live browser acceptance or full-branch CI.

This change does not include the separate deadline scheduling, post-plan escalation, grounded reminder presentation or task-extraction context changes.

topPRs.title: fix(phone): preserve paired turns and recover revoked sessions
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Paired phones could lose a submitted turn when the stream disconnected, reuse an obsolete same-host pairing attempt, or clear a valid credential when Android replayed the connection deep link.

This change preserves accepted turns across transport disconnects, maintains paired-session authority through completion, persists terminal generation outcomes for reconnect, and binds pairing retries to the server and entered code. Credential persistence can retry without consuming the one-time code again; same-target deep-link replay preserves the paired session. Unpaired disconnected requests retain their cancellation behavior.

Validation at integrated head `d172d7226a8e9b5b63f6eff7cc8a89a2ea8a7f12`: seven UI suites passed 194 tests, integrated agent pairing/readiness/failure-persistence suites passed 13 tests, and changed-file Biome passed. Full `bun run verify` passed 284/284 tasks and all final audits. The renderer build and full app capture passed 218/218 browser tests; all 24 manually flagged images plus desktop/mobile chat were inspected without a visual regression. Packaged OCR verified 208 views, zero broken, with four native-camera exemptions. Current-head hosted run 36630602979 passed all four checks; an additional Source checks rerun in 36628735628 is still running. The earlier renderer timeout is retained as a failed attempt, recovered by the completed renderer build and capture. These are source and browser-fixture results; this revised branch has not been installed on a physical phone.

topPRs.title: Wake the existing reminder task at durable deadlines
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Depends on #32931 (saved-reminder presentation). This independently stacked draft contains only the 17-file absolute task-wake change, without the one-shot escalation, Automations UI or extractor-context changes.

Reminder deadlines previously waited for the next roughly minute-long LifeOps maintenance pass. Let the existing task request an absolute wake, retaining the existing one-second core poll and task identity. SQL-backed adapters atomically keep the earliest deadline and increment a revision; completion consumes only the revision observed before execution, preserving concurrent earlier/equal requests. Pause, failure backoff and delivery eligibility remain authoritative.

LifeOps reconciles committed create/update/snooze changes, then derives the next deadline from the same effective plans, occurrences and attempts already used for dispatch. No second history scan, scheduler or queue is added. The wake mechanism introduces no model invocation; ordinary worker work still runs on each added pass. SQLite/custom adapters without atomic support explicitly retain ordinary cadence.

Cost: relevant mutations add an immediate reconciliation pass and atomic wake write; distinct deadlines may add further maintenance passes. Idle processing retains base cadence. Domain commit and wake write are separate, so crash recovery, processing limits, quiet gates or a busy worker can still delay delivery. Virtual-clock timing is not a live latency guarantee. No one-second delivery SLA is claimed.

Normal PR Validation does not automatically run on this feature-branch base. Full exact-head CI and live acceptance remain pending.

Validation on this independent stack: 31 focused tests passed (12 core wake/pause cases, 3 real SQL atomic-boundary cases, 13 personal-assistant unit/scheduler cases, 3 real reminder integrations). Covers equal-time/earlier request races, restart and passed-during-work deadlines, unsupported adapters, failure/pause precedence, malformed metadata, exact reminder-step identity, snooze and quiet-blocked no-spin behavior. Core build, core/SQL/personal-assistant typechecks, 17-file Biome and diff checks passed. No paid or live delivery test was run for this draft.

topPRs.title: fix(core): record background task model calls in trajectories
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Background workers could make model calls without an active trajectory step, leaving usage records without complete inputs and outputs. Establish a task-local capture scope and allocate the existing trajectory owner only at an actual model invocation. Preserve ambient privacy sessions, reuse active owners, and include PII escalation and instrumented raw calls.

Validation: all 14 real-PGlite persistence tests pass on the integrated head. They cover 100 idle executions with zero capture rows, complete large payloads, prepared secret/PII values, concurrent calls and task isolation, PII/embedding fallback, active owners, disabled recording, streaming completion/cancellation, and diagnostic failures without replaying business effects. Core typecheck and lint pass. This branch includes the workspace/fixture repair from #32934; full repository `bun run verify` passes at `8e56a14fb8e0dca6406079687ef158ed46fafa4f` (284 workspace build/typecheck/lint tasks plus all root audits). Hosted checks are still pending.

Tasks without captured model calls create no trajectory rows. Actual calls share one owner and use the existing flush/end lifecycle. This does not recover historical missing inputs or establish a latency improvement.

topPRs.title: fix(phone): expose remote local-model readiness accurately
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Remote chat could appear ready without usable local weights, but checking only resident weights also locked the composer after the idle timer unloaded a model that the provider can reload. Readiness now follows the generation provider's actual loader, desktop engine, and installed slot assignments without loading weights or invoking inference. HTTP health/status and initial/periodic WebSocket status carry the same readiness fields. History replay remains synchronous while the optional readiness probe runs.

The UI explains unavailable local weights and suppresses local-download warnings for phone sessions using a remote host. Connector names alone no longer identify a serving model. Mixed providers and unknown Cloud catalog status keep their existing behavior. Browser regressions cover missing-model startup and transition to ready on desktop and mobile while preserving an entered draft.

Validation: 38 provider tests, 7 authenticated HTTP/WebSocket tests, 219 UI tests, and 3 browser scenarios passed. The full app visual audit passed all 218 captures; OCR found no broken views, and all four camera exceptions were manually inspected as expected browser-unavailable states. Desktop/mobile readiness screenshots were inspected. Changed-file Biome passed. Final full root verification passed (284 tasks and repository audits); current-head hosted checks must pass before merge. The earlier standalone provider typecheck lacked generated assistant declarations; the integrated full build closure subsequently passed. This branch includes the reviewed workspace/fixture repair from #32934 and current develop. Physical phone hardware was not tested. Auth/reconnect changes remain in #32922.
